svg.title: Personal Agents OS: agent lifecycle and memory
svg.desc: An agent is a role spec in agents/<role>/ plus a private memory in data/agents/<role>/. It is created from a role or from agents/_template, onboards from the repo on its first turn, mirrors runner memory and routines into the repo in the same turn, commits its own paths, and the tech-maintainer audits it daily.
svg.text: An agent is a role with a memory
The spec is versioned in agents/<role>/, the memory is private in data/agents/<role>/, and the runner is replaceable.
In the repo · versioned, no personal data
the spec: name, persona, channel, reads, writes, requires;
then lane and handoffs, rules, memory, routines, flows
empty memory files: headings only, no facts
one spec per routine: schedule, status, intent, when silent,
the thin launcher: "/fitness-coach" or "talk to the fitness
the skeleton for a new role
Agreements · Open · Log, from the skeleton;
links person: "[[_me]]" so it is never an orphan
MEMORY LIVES IN THE REPO, NOT ONLY IN THE RUNNER
No fact may exist only in a runner:
One agent, one job: hand over to the
quietly, in the owner's own words.
Its own reads of the owner stay in
pull first; never git add -A, never
Keeps every agent honest: what a runner holds, the repo holds too.
Each routine is silent when green. Small mechanical fixes are reported in one line; structural changes only on the owner's yes.
Roles ship without names: the persona is generated by create_agent.py on your machine.
